cases.question: How much is Xero per month in Australia?
cases.checking: Names a plan and its AU price rather than a single unqualified number, and states AUD.
cases.answer: The Australian pricing passages list three plans, each showing a lower first-month price followed by a standard monthly price. Grow is $7.80 per month, then $78 per month (E3). cases.question: Is there a discount for new customers at the moment?
cases.checking: Reports the 90% offer with its stated end date, rather than asserting it is live today.
cases.answer: Yes — the passages describe new-customer discount offers in two regions. In Australia (prices in AUD, page retrieved 2026-09-14): new customers get 90% off for the first 3 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled; this is only available to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com, using code DC9032619AU, and the offer is available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026. The discount applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions and does not apply to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees, unless otherwise specified (E1). In the United States (prices in USD, page retrieved 2026-09-14): new customers get 90% off for the first 6 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled; this is only available to customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com using code DC90626308US, and the offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. The discount applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions and does not apply to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees, unless otherwise specified (E2). Both passages state the offer cannot be used with, or exchanged for, any other offer, and that Xero can change or cancel the offer at any time (E1, E2).
cases.notes: Region and currency matter here: E1 applies to Australia and is presented in AUD, and E2 applies to the United States and is presented in USD. Both pricing passages were retrieved on 2026-09-14, and each offer is stated as available until 30 September 2026 (11:59pm AEST for Australia; 11:59pm UTC for the US). The passages state offer terms and eligibility but do not state a 'current' date beyond the retrieval timestamps.

cases.answer:
The passages cover Australian and United States pricing pages plus an Australian accounting-software page, and they only partly answer the question.

Plans and pricing (Australia, AUD, as retrieved 2026-09-14, page region AU): the Australian pricing page names the plans Grow, Comprehensive and Ultimate 10 (E2). The Grow plan is shown at "$7.80 per month" then "$78 per month" (E2). Prices on that page "are in AUD and include GST", Xero "reserves the right to change pricing at any time", and subscriptions "auto-renew monthly until they are cancelled" (E2). A separate Australian page states that if you purchase any Xero plan you get the first month free (E4).

Plans and pricing (United States, USD, as retrieved 2026-09-14, page region US): the US page names the plans Early, Growing and Established (E3). The Early plan is shown at "$2.50 per month" then "$25 per month" (E3). On that page subscription prices are listed in USD and "do not include applicable taxes", taxes are calculated from your billing address, subscriptions auto-renew monthly, and you can switch to a less expensive plan 1 month after upgrading; it also states that "Xero subscription prices are increasing from October 1, 2026" (E3).

Features: the Australian Grow plan lists as included "Smart document capture basic extraction", "Payroll for 2 people", "60 day cashflow forecast" and "Claim expenses and mileage for 1 user" (E2). The same page shows feature/limit items including "Basic Extraction" marked Beta, forecasts of 60, 90 and 180 days, expense users in tiers ("For 1 user", "For 2 people"... "For 5 users"), "$5 per additional user" and "$7 per additional user" for additional users, "3 budgets", and "Up to 5", "Up to 10" and "Up to 15" bill-payment limits at "$0.35 per additional bill payment††" (E2). The US Early plan lists as included "Send quotes and 20 invoices†", "5 bills", "Reconcile bank transactions", "Visualize performance with basic graphs" and "30 day cash flow forecast" (E3). The US page also lists an optional item at "$36 a month + $6 per employee/contractor" without stating in the passage what that item is for (E3).

Invoicing and payroll: the US Early plan includes sending quotes and 20 invoices (E3). The Australian page states that Xero is "ATO-certified for STP", automatically calculates GST and generates "pre-filled activity statements" that can be lodged directly with the ATO (E6).

General features and trial: on the Australian accounting-software page, Xero is described as cloud-based accounting software that lets you log in wherever you have an internet connection, and it is said to help manage financial admin including tracking income and expenses, managing invoices, reconciling bank transactions and preparing financial reports (E6). Most banks can be connected automatically via a secure direct feed for daily updates, and where automatic bank feeds are not available you can manually import bank statements (E6). Xero "offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs" and the page directs users to the pricing page to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E6). Customer reviews on that page refer to automated bank feeds, invoicing features and easy reconciliation (E5).

The evidence does not give pricing for the Comprehensive or Ultimate 10 plans, does not give AU payroll pricing, and does not give feature details for the US Growing and Established plans beyond the comparison fragments shown.

E3 is a United States page, region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:18.157Z. All figures are as retrieved on those dates and are region- and time-specific. E2's section text appears to be a mixed capture of a plan comparison table, so some items are not clearly tied to a specific plan.
